newsitem.title: UK: Anglo-U.S. open skies talks to resume on Feb 4.
newsitem.headline: Anglo-U.S. open skies talks to resume on Feb 4.

text.p: Britain said on Thursday that it is to resume "open skies" trade talks next month aimed at opening up the transatlantic airline market to free competition.
A British government official said the Department of Transport's (DOT) negotiating team will be travelling to Washington for three days of talks on February 4.
Anglo-U.S. open skies talks to resume =2

The talks are closely linked to the proposed alliance between British Airways and American Airlines with both governments making an open skies agreement a condition for approving the controversial deal.

Airlines have been asked to submit comments by the end of this week to Britain's Office of Fair Trading (OFT) on British trade minister Ian Lang's proposals for approving the alliance which he announced at the end of the last round of open skies talks in London on December 5.

Meanwhile BA and American have said they are preparing to start the formal process of applying for approvals in the U.S. by making a joint filing of their planned alliance with the U.S. departments of Justice and Transportation.
Industry sources said there was speculation that the filing could be made in Washington on Friday.
The two airlines said today that they plan to hold a news conference in Washington at 1500 GMT tomorrow to make "an important announcment" but declined to comment further.
Under the proposed alliance BA intends to coordinate its 244 flights a week to 22 U.S. destinations with American's 238 flights from seven U.S. airports to 12 European destinations.
